backlog.spec: Increase N_TREES from 300 to 1000 to capture more complex patterns in the data. This might increase runtime but should improve generalization.
backlog.title: Increase N_TREES

backlog.spec: Change MAX_FEATURES to 0.1. Since Morgan fingerprints are sparse, limiting the number of features considered at each split can reduce noise and improve stability.
backlog.title: Reduce MAX_FEATURES

backlog.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 5 to prevent the trees from over-fitting to noise in individual molecules, especially since the dataset is small.
backlog.title: Increase MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with XGBRegressor. XGBoost often performs better than Random Forest for tabular data by using gradient boosting.
backlog.title: Switch to XGBoost

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with LightGBM. LightGBM is often faster and more memory-efficient than XGBoost for large numbers of features.
backlog.title: Switch to LightGBM

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with CatBoostRegressor. CatBoost is known to handle categorical/sparse data very well and often provides excellent out-of-the-box performance.
backlog.title: Switch to CatBoost

backlog.spec: Apply StandardScaler to the target variable (train_y) before training and inverse transform the predictions. This might help some gradient-based models converge better.
backlog.title: Target Scaling (StandardScaler)

backlog.spec: Apply RobustScaler to the target variable to handle potential outliers in the logD measurements more effectively than StandardScaler.
backlog.title: Target Scaling (RobustScaler)

backlog.spec: While the final score is MAE, some models perform better when optimized for MSE. If using XGB/LightGBM, ensure the objective is tuned for regression.
backlog.title: Use mean squared error loss

backlog.spec: Increase RADIUS from 2 to 3. This captures more global chemical context but increases the dimensionality and complexity of the fingerprints.
backlog.title: Increase Radius

backlog.spec: Reduce N_BITS from 2048 to 1024 to see if the reduced dimensionality reduces noise in the small dataset.
backlog.title: Reduce N_BITS

backlog.spec: Augment the featurize function to include the molecular weight as an additional feature, as it is highly correlated with lipophilicity.
backlog.title: Add Molecule Weight

backlog.spec: Augment the featurize function to include the count of hydrogen atoms as an additional feature.
backlog.title: Add Hydrogen Count

backlog.spec: Apply a log transformation to the target values if they are skewed. However, since logD is already logarithmic, check if a sqrt transform or other mild non-linear transform helps.
backlog.title: Log Transform Target

backlog.spec: If using XGBRegressor, set subsample to 0.8 to introduce randomness and prevent the model from over-focusing on specific training samples.
backlog.title: XGBoost with subsample

backlog.spec: If using XGBRegressor, set colsample_bytree to 0.8 to ensure each tree only sees a subset of the 2048 bits.
backlog.title: XGBoost with colsample_bytree

backlog.spec: If using LightGBM, set feature_fraction to 0.8 to perform column subsampling during the boosting process.
backlog.title: LightGBM with feature_fraction

backlog.spec: If using CatBoostRegressor, set max_depth to 6. A shallower tree can be more robust on small datasets.
backlog.title: CatBoost with depth

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with ExtraTreesRegressor. It introduces more randomness by choosing random thresholds for features.
backlog.title: Use ExtraTreesRegressor

backlog.spec: Train three different models (RF, XGB, CatBoost) and average their predictions (simple ensemble).
backlog.title: Multi-layered Ensemble

backlog.spec: Use RDKit's Descriptors to add TPSA to the feature vector. TPSA is a standard descriptor for lipophilicity-related properties.
backlog.title: Add Topological Polar Surface Area (TPSA)

backlog.spec: Add the count of rings as a scalar feature to the featurize function.
backlog.title: Add Number of Rings

backlog.spec: Use RDKit's Wildman-Crippen LogP (Wildman-Crippen method) as a feature. It's a very strong proxy for logD.
backlog.title: Add LogP (estimated)

backlog.spec: For Random Forest, explicitly set max_depth to 20. This limits the depth of individual trees.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter Tuning: Max Depth

backlog.spec: Set min_samples_split to 5 for the Random Forest model.
backlog.title: Hyperparameter Tuning: Min Samples Split

backlog.spec: Convert the output of featurize to a sparse matrix (scipy.sparse.csr_matrix) to save memory and potentially speed up training for large models.
backlog.title: Use Sparse Matrix

backlog.spec: Implement a simple internal 3-fold cross-validation within fit_predict to select the best of N different seeds, then return the best model.
backlog.title: Cross-validation local check

backlog.spec: Reduce N_TREES to 100 to see if the model is significantly over-fitting and if a simpler model provides similar accuracy.
backlog.title: Reduce Number of Trees

backlog.spec: Randomly select a subset of the 2048 bits (e.g., 1024) each time fit_predict is called to simulate a bagging approach on features.
backlog.title: Randomize Feature Selection

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with ExtraTreesRegressor. ExtraTrees uses more randomization by selecting a different random subset of features for every split, which can help reduce variance and improve generalization in some chemical datasets. Use the same N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES, and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF parameters.
backlog.title: Use ExtraTreesRegressor

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with XGBoost's XGBRegressor. Use a reasonable number of estimators (e.g., 300) and set learning_rate=0.1. Ensure the seed is passed correctly and use n_jobs=-1 to utilize all 8 threads.
backlog.title: Switch to XGBoost

backlog.spec: Replace RandomForestRegressor with LightGBM's LGBMRegressor. Set n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.1, and number_of_leaf=31. Use the seed for random_state and n_jobs=-1.
backlog.title: Switch to LightGBM

backlog.spec: Apply np.log1p to the train_y values before fitting the model and then use np.expm1 to transform the predictions back to the original scale. Log transformation is often beneficial for logD values which can have skewed distributions.
backlog.title: Use Log Transformation on Target

backlog.spec: Decrease the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 1. A smaller radius captures more local environment information and may act as a form of regularization by reducing the complexity of the features.
backlog.title: Reduce Morgan Fingerprint Radius

backlog.spec: Decrease N_BITS from 2048 to 1024. Reducing the dimensionality of the fingerprint can help the Random Forest generalize better by forcing the model to find the most significant features in a smaller space.
backlog.title: Reduce Number of Bits

backlog.spec: Use sklearn.preprocessing.RobustScaler to scale train_y before fitting the model, and use the same scaler's transform method on the predictions. RobustScaler is less sensitive to outliers than StandardScaler.
backlog.title: Target Scaling with RobustScaler

backlog.spec: Switch to XGBRegressor and set colsample_bytree=0.8 and subsample=0.8. These parameters introduce stochasticity into the boosting process, which can significantly improve generalization on small datasets.
backlog.title: XGBoost with Feature Subsampling

backlog.spec: Switch to LGBMRegressor and set feature_fraction=0.8 and bag_fraction=0.8. Similar to XGBoost, these introduce randomness to prevent the model from over-relying on specific high-impact features.
backlog.title: LightGBM with Feature Fraction

backlog.spec: Introduce a small amount of noise to the features by randomly setting a small percentage (e.g., 5%) of the fingerprint bits to zero (or random values) during each fit_predict call, or use a smaller MAX_FEATURES value like 0.1.
backlog.title: Randomize Feature Selection

backlog.spec: Apply a log1p transformation to the target values (train_y) before training, as logD values often follow a skewed distribution. Note that since logD is already a log value, this is technically a double-log, but if the distribution is severely non-normal, it can help the model focus on relative differences. If the target is already centered, use StandardScaler instead.
backlog.title: Log-transform Target Variable

backlog.spec: Decrease N_TREES to 1000 and introduce learning_rate=0.05. Explicitly set num_leaves=31 (the default) or experiment with 63. This moves away from the default 'fast' setting to a more controlled learning process for the LightGBMRegressor.
backlog.title: Optimize LightGBM Learning Rate and Leaves

backlog.spec: After featurizing the SMILES into a NumPy array of bits, apply StandardScalar from scikit-learn to the feature matrix before training the LightGBMRegressor. This helps the gradient boosting algorithm converge more stably by centering the feature space.
backlog.title: Standardize Morgan Fingerprints

backlog.spec: Modify the featurize function to concatenate the 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint with a small set of counts: Number of Heavy Atoms, Number of Rings, and number of Oxygen atoms. This provides global molecular context that fingerprints might miss.
backlog.title: Hybrid Morgan + Count Features

backlog.spec: Modify fit_predict to split the training data into a 90/10 split internally. Use the LightGBM 'early_stopping' callback (requires a validation set) to stop training when the loss stops decreasing, preventing overfitting on the 3360 molecules.
backlog.title: Early Stopping with Validation Set

backlog.spec: Replace LightGBMRegressor with CatBoostRegressor. Set iterations=1000, learning_rate=0.05, depth=6, and random_strength=1. CatBoost is often robust to noise and may handle the chemical fingerprint data differently than the tree-based gradient boosting of LightGBM.
backlog.title: Switch to CatBoostRegressor

backlog.spec: Replace the current model with XGBRegressor. Use max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, and subsample=0.8. Ensure use of the seed for random_state. XGBoost handles the sparse/binary nature of fingerprints very efficiently.
backlog.title: Switch to XGBRegressor with DMatrix

backlog.spec: Set RADIUS=3 and N_BITS=1024. This captures larger chemical environments while the bit reduction forces the model to generalize on more compressed, salient chemical information.
backlog.title: Increase Radius to 3 with Bit Reduction

backlog.spec: Use 'from rdkit import Descriptors' to calculate MolWt, XLogP, and TPSA. Append these 3 float values to the end of the featurized Morgan fingerprint array. This provides physical chemical descriptors that directly correlate with lipophilicity.
backlog.title: Add RDKit Descriptors via Descriptors Module

backlog.spec: Modify fit_predict to train 3 separate LightGBMRegressor models with different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) and average their predictions. Ensembling is a standard way to reduce the variance of the 5-fold CV score.
backlog.title: Small Ensemble: 3x LightGBM Average
